strategy.observation: Canva has launched its Creative Operating System, a major AI-powered foundation across the Visual Suite, and Canva’s platform includes templates plus AI tools for creating presentations, docs, videos, and more.
strategy.offer_link: Because the new connected Visual Suite appears to broaden the number and variety of templates people can use, accessibility audits against WCAG 2.2 could help catch issues before template changes or new template sets ship across Canva’s products.
hypotheses: The Creative Operating System rollout is increasing the pace at which templates and template-adjacent assets change.
The Head of Accessibility may be responsible for setting quality standards for templates across multiple content types, not just core app UI.
Canva may want to ensure templates used by enterprise customers are safe to publish at scale without accessibility regressions.
strategy.angle: With Canva’s new Creative Operating System tying templates across the Visual Suite, every template update now has a broader accessibility surface area.
strategy.fit_reason: Canva’s product is template-heavy and spans multiple content formats, so WCAG 2.2 audits of design templates have a plausible, concrete use: finding and preventing accessibility issues in assets that are likely to be reused at scale across the platform.

draft.subject: Templates across Visual Suite
draft.body:
With Canva’s new Creative Operating System tying templates across the Visual Suite, the accessibility surface area looks a lot bigger. If template updates are moving faster too, my guess is a WCAG 2.2 review before release could catch issues earlier, especially across presentations, docs, and video templates.

I audit design templates against WCAG 2.2, mainly to flag problems before they get repeated at scale. Which template family would you want checked first if you were tightening accessibility coverage across the suite?
